issues.title: EV retail is growing. Is your service handoff ready?
issues.summary: FADA's 6 November statement reports about 3.55 lakh electric-vehicle registrations across all categories in October 2026. New registrations are not workshop visits. The useful question is whether the service team can identify electrified vehicles, route them safely and keep customer promises.
issues.sourceNote: FADA's October 2026 retail-registration statement dated 6 November 2026, covering 1–31 October. The first-party release text was verified through a syndicated reproduction and independent reporting; a direct FADA-hosted October PDF was not accessible for examination. Figures are registrations, NOT OEM wholesales or repair orders.

metrics.label: EV registrations, all categories
metrics.context: FADA statement • October 2026 • approximate retail count

metrics.label: Electric share of PV registrations
metrics.context: FADA retail powertrain mix • October 2026 • PV denominator

metrics.label: Passenger-vehicle retail registrations
metrics.context: India • October 2026 • not OEM wholesale dispatches

issues.reportingType: FADA-reported retail registrations for 1–31 October 2026; not manufacturer wholesales, workshop inflow, or a dealer-level survey
intro: The number worth noticing is not a workshop target. FADA's 6 November 2026 statement says electric-vehicle retail registrations reached approximately 3.55 lakh across vehicle categories in October 2026. Within passenger vehicles, electric models represented 7.30% of 5,07,768 retail registrations. These are two different denominators.

A registered vehicle is not a service visit. It would be misleading to turn a month's EV retail data into a forecast for service revenue, trained-technician demand or diagnostic failures. But the changing mix is a useful reason to audit how enquiries and repair orders are received, identified and handed to the right people.

For the next EV or hybrid customer, can the advisor capture the exact vehicle and complaint, can the workshop assign work only within its training and equipment limits, and can the customer get a realistic update? That is the operational test, not a slogan about electrification.

interpretation.heading: Prepare the service process before the next exception
points: Identify the powertrain and exact vehicle/VIN at appointment and job-card creation; do not treat EV, hybrid and conventional vehicles as interchangeable.

For work involving high-voltage systems, follow the manufacturer procedure and route only to authorised, appropriately trained personnel; escalate otherwise. This is a safety and process recommendation, not a claim about an industry-wide skills gap.
Agree on parts availability, diagnostic authorisation, expected completion and next customer-update time before making a delivery promise.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Explain ownership support at handover
desks.check: For each EV delivery, verify that the customer receives model-specific charging, roadside assistance, warranty and service-booking guidance.
desks.metric: EV deliveries with recorded customer orientation ÷ EV deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A useful handover reduces avoidable confusion over whom to contact for help.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Route the job to the right technician
desks.check: Review electrified-vehicle job cards for VIN/powertrain identification, a named trained owner and safe escalation where high-voltage competence or equipment is unavailable.
desks.metric: EV/hybrid ROs with documented qualified assignment and triage ÷ EV/hybrid ROs (%)
desks.rationale: Good routing protects safety and reduces unowned diagnostic delays.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Confirm fitment before quoting
desks.check: For an electrified-vehicle parts request, match VIN and part number and record availability, supersession and supplier ETA before promising completion.
desks.metric: EV/hybrid parts requests with verified VIN and ETA ÷ EV/hybrid parts requests (%)
desks.rationale: A wrong or delayed component can keep a specialist bay occupied.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Document battery and warranty evidence
desks.check: Before acquiring a used EV, record the VIN, warranty eligibility, charging accessories and an OEM-supported battery assessment where available.
desks.metric: Used EV appraisals with battery/warranty evidence ÷ used EV appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: Unknown battery or warranty status makes an appraisal unnecessarily speculative.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Track outstanding electrified-vehicle claims
desks.check: Review EV/hybrid warranty claims for complete invoices, approvals, labour documentation and payment status; assign owners to overdue cases.
desks.metric: Value of EV/hybrid warranty claims outstanding over 30 days (₹)
desks.rationale: Correct technical work still needs timely claim documentation and reconciliation.

issues.huddleTitle: One electrified-vehicle case. Five clean handoffs.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real EV or hybrid case; if none is currently open, use the latest genuine customer enquiry. Record an owner, the next step and a deadline; never perform high-voltage work as part of the huddle.
huddle: Minutes 0–3: Sales checks what ownership, warranty and service guidance the customer received.
Minutes 3–6: Service confirms VIN, complaint, trained assignment and any safety/escalation limit.
Minutes 6–9: Spares validates any requested part number, fitment and availability.
Minutes 9–12: Used Cars checks what evidence would be needed if this vehicle came in for exchange.
Minutes 12–15: Accounts checks claim/billing documentation and the team records one owner, deadline and customer update.
limitations: FADA's statement, dated 6 November 2026, concerns October 1–31 retail registrations. No November registrations, future sales or aftersales RO volumes are inferred.
The approximately 3.55 lakh EV figure covers all vehicle categories. The 7.30% EV figure is a share of PASSENGER-VEHICLE retail registrations; the percentages are not interchangeable.

The October release was not available as a directly inspected PDF on the FADA domain (site access blocked); its FADA-authored statement was checked in a syndicated reproduction and its major figures corroborated by independent dated trade coverage. Original publisher-hosted document and RTO scope/coverage footnotes remain unverified; retain an approval hold.
Monthly retail-registration figures are not manufacturer wholesale dispatches, billings, cash collections, service visits, repair demand or evidence of staff competency gaps.
FADA attributes the October 2026 year-on-year comparison to the unusual festival calendar; this issue does not infer a measured service-workload effect.

All five desk checks and suggested metrics are original RPHV guidance, not FADA standards or mandatory manufacturer service procedures. Follow the applicable OEM safety directions; do not attempt high-voltage work without appropriate training/authorisation.
If no relevant EV/hybrid cases occurred, record the metric as not applicable, not 100%.

issues.title: Festive sales: the dates can change the story.
issues.summary: FADA's provisional Navratri passenger-vehicle registrations were 10.39% higher than in 2024 but 21.91% lower than in 2025. The two comparisons use different festival windows. Before revising targets, separate calendar effects from the dealership's actual enquiry-to-delivery performance.
issues.sourceNote: FADA provisional vehicle retail-registration release, published 21 October 2026; Navratri 2026 covers 11-20 October (10 days), versus 22 September-2 October 2025 (11 days) and 3-12 October 2024 (10 days). These are customer registrations, not OEM wholesales.

metrics.label: PV retail registrations
metrics.context: India; Navratri 2026, 11-20 October; provisional FADA data

metrics.label: PV registrations vs Navratri 2024
metrics.context: Both festival windows covered 10 days; 1,65,534 in 2024

metrics.label: PV registrations vs Navratri 2025
metrics.context: 2025 covered 11 days; 2,34,004 registrations; not like-for-like

issues.reportingType: Provisional customer vehicle registrations (FADA/MoRTH); not manufacturer wholesales, dealer invoicing, or a representative enquiry survey
intro: The headline depends on the comparison chosen. In its 21 October release, FADA recorded 1,82,728 passenger-vehicle registrations during Navratri 2026 (11-20 October). That was 10.39% above the 1,65,534 registrations recorded across the ten-day 2024 Navratri period, yet 21.91% below the 2,34,004 recorded during Navratri 2025.

The 2025 festival window ran for eleven days (22 September-2 October), compared with ten days in 2026 and 2024. FADA also identified the September 2025 GST changes and accumulated demand as factors that made last year's base unusual. The reported decline should therefore not be treated as a clean measure of weakened customer interest.

For a dealership, the more useful question is operational: Of customers promising a festive delivery, how many cars are allocated, finance-cleared, registered and actually ready to hand over? Review that chain before changing discounts, staffing or purchase decisions. Registrations reflect retail activity; OEM dispatches are a different data series.

interpretation.heading: Read the market. Then inspect your own funnel.
points: Compare matched days or clearly label uneven festival windows; also examine the same dealership's week-by-week enquiry, booking and delivery stages.
For the coming seven days, verify every promised delivery against vehicle allocation, finance status, registration and required fitments. A booking is not a confirmed handover.
Record why each deferred delivery slipped: customer request, allocation, documents, finance, PDI or accessories. The reason tells managers which process to improve.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check the promised delivery, not just the booking
desks.check: For all deliveries promised within seven days, confirm the customer's date, available VIN, finance approval and registration progress.
desks.metric: Fully confirmed deliveries ÷ deliveries promised in next 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: This identifies promises at risk without confusing industry registrations with your own sales funnel.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Release cars only after PDI closure
desks.check: Match every planned handover VIN to a completed pre-delivery inspection and closure of any safety or functional defects.
desks.metric: Deliveries with completed, signed PDI ÷ total deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: An incomplete inspection can turn a festive delivery into an early complaint.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Flag accessories holding up handovers
desks.check: Review accessories and fitments promised for the next seven days; verify kit availability, technician slot and supplier ETA.
desks.metric: Deliveries with all promised accessories ready before handover ÷ deliveries requiring accessories (%)
desks.rationale: Missing fitments create preventable delays and broken customer commitments.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Close exchange appraisals before the delivery date
desks.check: Identify upcoming deliveries with exchange commitments; confirm physical appraisal, ownership paperwork and approved trade-in value.
desks.metric: Exchange-linked deliveries with signed-off appraisals ÷ exchange-linked deliveries due (%)
desks.rationale: Unresolved exchange values can prevent a confirmed new-vehicle handover.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Clear money and documents before release
desks.check: Reconcile advances, lender payout confirmation, invoice balance and statutory charges on each delivery-due file.
desks.metric: Scheduled deliveries fully payment-cleared before handover ÷ scheduled deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A delivery is operationally complete only when financial and documentation controls are clear.

issues.huddleTitle: Five desks. One delivery at risk. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real delivery file to identify the single blocker that could disappoint the customer, then assign its owner and deadline.
huddle: Minutes 0-3: Sales checks customer commitment, allocation and confirmed date.
Minutes 3-6: Service validates the VIN's PDI and any open defect.
Minutes 6-9: Spares confirms accessories, fitment slot and any part ETA.
Minutes 9-12: Used Cars clears exchange valuation and transfer paperwork, if applicable.
Minutes 12-15: Accounts confirms payment and registration-related clearance; record the owner and customer update time.
limitations: FADA's 21 October report was provisional. Retail data were collated as of 21 October 2026 from 1,468 of 1,469 RTOs in collaboration with MoRTH; figures can change with late registrations or revisions.

The festival windows differ: 2026 (11-20 Oct, 10 days), 2025 (22 Sep-2 Oct, 11 days), 2024 (3-12 Oct, 10 days). The -21.91% 2025 comparison is not a like-for-like daily or calendar-month growth measure.

FADA notes that Telangana registration data for 3W, CV and tractor categories were unavailable for Navratri 2026; this caveat applies to relevant all-vehicle totals, though PV is not listed among the missing categories.

FADA's discussion of GST-linked pent-up demand is industry interpretation, not causal proof about every dealership. Festival registrations cannot establish dealership enquiry conversion or profitability.

This article contains no October 2026 full-month FADA retail figure. It does not combine festival retail registrations with October manufacturer wholesale dispatches as if they describe the same period.
The five practical checks, metrics and 15-minute huddle are original RPHV operational suggestions, not FADA or OEM performance standards.

issues.title: Used-car buying is going phygital. Trust still needs a paper trail.
issues.summary: A newly announced physical-plus-digital used-car partnership combines online discovery with dealership inspections, finance and handover. The opportunity is real; the dealer's test is whether every vehicle has a verifiable ownership, condition and cost file before money changes hands.
issues.sourceNote: Landmark Cars and OLX India corporate partnership announcement, 24 September 2026. It describes a planned phased rollout and company-reported network footprint at announcement date; it is not a monthly sales report.

metrics.label: Retail and service touchpoints
metrics.context: Landmark network, company-stated in 24 Sep 2026 release; not used-car-only locations

metrics.label: Indian states in stated network
metrics.context: Company-reported existing footprint at announcement

metrics.label: Proposed rollout
metrics.context: Selected cities first; no completed nationwide rollout claimed

issues.reportingType: Corporate strategy announcement; neither vehicle wholesales nor retail registrations
intro: In a 24 September 2026 stock-exchange-disclosed announcement, Landmark Cars and OLX India outlined a partnership intended to connect digital pre-owned-car discovery with physical inspections, test drives, financing, ownership transfer and post-sale support. It is a proposed operating model, not a report of vehicles sold.

Landmark said its existing retail and service network spanned more than 140 touchpoints across 12 states. That is a company-described network footprint, not the number of used-car outlets operating under the new arrangement. The rollout was described as phased, beginning in selected cities.

For an independent dealership or used-car desk, the broader lesson is practical. Technology may attract and match a buyer, but a trustworthy transaction still depends on the VIN, legal ownership, condition report, repair estimate, finance closure and documented handover.

interpretation.heading: What this changes for an ordinary dealer
points: Treat an online lead as the beginning of a verified transaction, not proof that a vehicle is ready to buy or deliver.
Use a standard vehicle dossier linking VIN, inspection photos, test-drive findings, pending repairs, document status and customer approvals.
Track the complete acquisition-to-handover cycle and contribution margin rather than only advertised selling price.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Book the appraisal before offering exchange value
desks.check: Check today's exchange enquiries for an identified vehicle, available RC details and a confirmed appraisal appointment.
desks.metric: Exchange enquiries with appraisal appointments ÷ total exchange enquiries (%)
desks.rationale: A price promise without verified vehicle details creates avoidable disputes.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Document condition before negotiation
desks.check: Verify that each considered trade-in has a signed inspection covering safety items, accident indicators, engine/transmission condition and an estimated repair list.
desks.metric: Appraised vehicles with completed inspection sheets ÷ total appraised vehicles (%)
desks.rationale: An inspection that cannot be reproduced is a weak basis for valuation.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Price the reconditioning basket
desks.check: Confirm part numbers, availability and supplier ETA for every material repair item in the vehicle appraisal.
desks.metric: Reconditioning estimates with confirmed parts price and ETA (%)
desks.rationale: A low purchase price can still hide costly or delayed repairs.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Require a verified vehicle dossier
desks.check: Before paying for a vehicle, confirm the VIN against RC, owner/finance status, inspection report, known repair history and agreed transfer responsibilities.
desks.metric: Acquisitions with complete pre-payment dossiers ÷ total acquisitions (%)
desks.rationale: Document confidence and ownership transfer are central to customer trust.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Approve the full cost, not just the buying price
desks.check: Build a unit-level margin sheet including purchase, repairs, statutory/transfer-related costs, brokerage, finance and likely holding expense.
desks.metric: Units with signed-off estimated net margin before purchase (%)
desks.rationale: Gross resale spread is not the same as net profit.

issues.huddleTitle: One exchange car. Five checks. One decision.
issues.huddleSummary: Bring a live trade-in file to a 15-minute cross-functional review. Find the missing facts, not the person to blame.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales confirms customer consent, enquiry source, expected exchange date and appraisal slot.
Minutes 3–6 — Service identifies one unresolved condition or safety check and its inspection owner.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares verifies the highest-risk repair part, price and availability.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars confirms RC/VIN match, finance closure and ownership-transfer plan.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts validates estimated total cost and margin; the team records accept, hold or decline with an owner.
limitations: The September 24 announcement described a proposed partnership and phased rollout. It does not establish completed used-car sales, transaction quality, success rates, or a nationwide launch.
The 140+ touchpoints and 12-state footprint are company-reported Landmark network descriptors, not a count of dedicated used-car outlets.
No Indian used-car retail-registration volume is inferred. The release is not OEM wholesale data, FADA/VAHAN registration data or a representative market survey.
The press release's online audience claims are intentionally excluded because marketplace visitors, buyers/sellers, listings and completed transactions are distinct measures.
Department checks and suggested metrics are RPHV editorial recommendations, not government or OEM benchmarks.

The original exchange-announcement metadata and the issuer's investor-relations index were identified. The linked original PDF attachment could not be inspected in full in this drafting run; publication requires a final attachment check.

issues.title: The aftermarket is growing. Is the right part on your shelf?
issues.summary: ACMA reports a 9% increase in India's domestic auto-component aftermarket in FY2025-26. For dealerships, bigger industry demand is no substitute for correct part identification, reliable order ETAs and disciplined inventory.
issues.sourceNote: ACMA's FY2025-26 industry review is listed in its official press archive on 17 July 2026; figures cross-checked against ACMA's undated live industry summary. Reporting period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. These are component-industry value indicators, not vehicle wholesales or retail registrations.

metrics.label: Domestic component aftermarket growth
metrics.context: India • FY2025-26 vs FY2024-25 • ACMA • value

metrics.label: Auto-component industry turnover growth
metrics.context: India • FY2025-26 vs FY2024-25 • ACMA • value

metrics.label: EV-component share of domestic OEM supplies
metrics.context: FY2025-26 • ACMA • excludes lithium-ion batteries

issues.reportingType: Auto-component industry value data, not vehicle wholesales or customer registrations
intro: India's auto-component business is expanding. ACMA reports that domestic aftermarket value grew 9% in FY2025-26 compared with FY2024-25, while total auto-component industry turnover grew 12.7%. ACMA also identifies EV components, excluding lithium-ion batteries, as 4.6% of domestic OEM component supplies.

These numbers have different denominators. The aftermarket figure is about replacement-parts market value; the 12.7% figure is about the wider components industry; the EV share refers to original-equipment component supplies. None measures dealer fill rate, repair delays, vehicle dispatches or retail registrations.

That distinction matters. A parts counter can be busy yet lose time and money through wrong variants, old superseded numbers, unconfirmed arrival dates and stock that never turns. Growth creates opportunity; process determines whether a workshop captures it.

interpretation.heading: Do not turn market growth into blind reordering
points: Build stock decisions from local repair history, model and powertrain mix, and actual demand—not an industry growth percentage.
Use VIN-based part identification, supersession checks and confirmed supplier lead times before promising completion dates.
Separate fast-moving service parts from high-value, low-frequency components so both customer waiting time and working capital remain visible.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Capture the exact vehicle variant
desks.check: Check five recent deliveries for complete VIN, model, year and powertrain details in the service/CRM record.
desks.metric: Delivery records with complete vehicle identification / deliveries checked (%)
desks.rationale: Accurate vehicle data reduces avoidable part-selection mistakes later.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Find the repairs stalled for parts
desks.check: Review parts-blocked repair orders; confirm part number, revised ETA, customer update and responsible person.
desks.metric: Open repair orders blocked for parts for over 48 hours (count)
desks.rationale: The 48-hour trigger is a suggested local escalation threshold, not an OEM standard.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Verify before you reorder
desks.check: Audit ten live parts orders against VIN/catalogue fitment, supersession, quantity and supplier confirmation.
desks.metric: Wrong-part returns / total parts issues in the review period (%)
desks.rationale: Correct fitment and first-time fill are more useful than ordering faster.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Cost variant-specific repairs early
desks.check: Before purchasing an exchange car, validate availability and price of required reconditioning parts.
desks.metric: Acquired units with signed, costed reconditioning sheets / acquired units (%)
desks.rationale: A cheap acquisition can become costly when repair parts are unavailable.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace money paid for parts not received
desks.check: Match supplier advances against open purchase orders, receipts and promised delivery dates.
desks.metric: Value of supplier advances for parts pending over 7 days (₹)
desks.rationale: A seven-day ageing flag is a management prompt, not a statutory threshold.

issues.huddleTitle: One delayed part. Five clear decisions.
issues.huddleSummary: Pick one real parts-blocked job. In 15 minutes, identify the fitment evidence, ETA, customer commitment and financial exposure.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: confirm VIN, model, powertrain and customer commitment.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: confirm symptom, diagnosis, part need and revised repair promise.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: validate part number, supersession, stock and supplier ETA.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: check whether any affected exchange/refurbishment job needs the same part and price update.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: confirm advance/credit exposure; assign the final owner and update deadline.
limitations: ACMA's July 2026 annual-industry press-archive entry covers FY2025-26 (1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026), not October or November 2026.

ACMA's current About page does not state its own publication/update date. The original downloadable annual release is linked from the archive but was not machine-readable in this review; percentage figures were cross-checked on ACMA's own live summary.

ACMA's live About page reports a domestic-aftermarket rupee amount that conflicts with other published FY26 reporting; this edition deliberately omits the disputed rupee value rather than presenting it as verified.
The reported +9% and +12.7% are value-growth rates with different industry scopes, while 4.6% is an OEM component-supply share excluding lithium-ion batteries; these should not be combined.
No October 2026 vehicle wholesale or retail-registration total is cited. No industry metric predicts a specific dealership's parts demand, customer waiting time or profitability.
The five operational checks, ratios, seven-day and 48-hour triggers are RPHV editorial recommendations, not published ACMA targets or legal standards.

sources.type: Primary industry association archive; values verified against ACMA live industry summary

issues.title: Record dispatches. What has actually turned into cash?
issues.summary: October's manufacturer sales releases show strong vehicle movement. But a wholesale headline is not a dealership's retail registration, stock turn or bank balance. This week's most useful question is which vehicles, repair jobs and claims have genuinely converted into collected money.
issues.sourceNote: Original Maruti Suzuki press release dated 1 November 2026 and Mahindra newsroom release page dated 2 November 2026 (its text carries a 1 November dateline), both reporting October 2026 manufacturer sales. These are company-reported dispatch/sales figures—not nationwide retail registrations, dealer deliveries or dealer cash receipts.

metrics.label: Maruti Suzuki total vehicle sales
metrics.context: October 2026; includes domestic sales, sales to other OEMs and exports; OEM-reported

metrics.label: Maruti Suzuki export volumes
metrics.context: October 2026; already included in its 2,76,120 total; not Indian retail

metrics.label: Mahindra domestic utility vehicles
metrics.context: October 2026; company-reported domestic UV sales, including subsidiary vehicles

issues.reportingType: Two manufacturers' October 2026 sales/dispatch releases (wholesale-related data); NOT customer retail registrations or nationwide market totals.
intro: Two fresh October releases offer a useful lesson in reading automotive numbers. Maruti Suzuki reported total vehicle sales of 2,76,120 units: 2,16,789 domestic sales (including its light commercial vehicles), 9,459 units supplied to other OEMs and 49,872 exports. Mahindra reported 73,338 domestic utility-vehicle sales in the same month. These are different company-specific categories; they must not be added together or treated as India's retail registrations.

For a dealer, the gap between manufacturer billing and customer delivery matters more than the size of a market headline. Vehicles can arrive, create inventory and financing exposure, and still wait for documentation, loan clearance, accessories or final settlement. Similarly, a closed repair order or a manufacturer claim is not cash until its billing and collection are reconciled.

Use the next quarter-hour to compare what was billed, what was delivered and what was collected. If any figure is missing, assign an owner to close that gap rather than debating whether the market is strong.

interpretation.heading: The operating lesson: build a stock-to-cash bridge
points: Keep OEM wholesale invoices, dealer retail registrations, physical deliveries and customer receipts in separate columns. They record different events and often different dates.
Identify vehicles with invoices or stock funding already booked but delivery or payment still pending. Separate genuine bottlenecks from paperwork delays.
Run the same exception discipline through open repair orders, ordered parts, exchange-car acquisition costs and unsettled claims. Report the number and age of exceptions, not just gross turnover.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Reconcile every promised handover
desks.check: Review the next seven days' vehicle deliveries: confirm allocation, registration, payment clearance and handover documents against the promised date.
desks.metric: Delivery-ready units / units promised for next 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: An allocated or invoiced vehicle has not necessarily reached the customer.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Stop completed jobs waiting for billing
desks.check: Check completed repair orders not yet invoiced or delivered; identify missing final QC, approvals or customer communication.
desks.metric: Completed ROs awaiting invoice or delivery over 24 hours (count)
desks.rationale: Workshop productivity is only one step toward realised revenue.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Match inventory to real job demand
desks.check: Take the top five high-value parts purchased but not issued and verify each job reservation, physical location and expected use date.
desks.metric: Unissued purchased-parts value older than 30 days (₹)
desks.rationale: Paid-for stock without a defined job can quietly absorb cash.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Know total cost before listing
desks.check: Check one exchange vehicle's agreed purchase value, transfer papers, repair estimate, carrying cost and approved asking price.
desks.metric: Acquired cars with complete cost-and-margin sheet / total acquired cars (%)
desks.rationale: A healthy resale price is not automatically a healthy gross margin.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Show cash gaps by owner and age
desks.check: Reconcile yesterday's vehicle receipts, workshop collections, unsettled OEM claims and stock-funding debits; allocate every unmatched item.
desks.metric: Unreconciled receipts and claims over 7 days (₹)
desks.rationale: A visible pending balance can be followed up before it becomes an ageing problem.

issues.huddleTitle: From invoice to bank: close five gaps
issues.huddleSummary: Five desks each bring one real exception. Record the amount or vehicle/RO number, the blocker, an accountable person and a dated next action.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: pick one billed or allocated vehicle with delayed delivery; identify the exact blocker.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: pick one completed but unbilled RO; agree the next step and responsible person.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: identify one paid-for part not issued to its intended job; confirm its status.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: review one exchange vehicle with unapproved reconditioning cost or margin.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: reconcile one unmatched receipt or ageing claim and set a deadline.
limitations: The two OEM releases cover October 1–31, 2026 manufacturer-reported sales. They do not report VAHAN customer retail registrations, dealer delivery counts or dealer cash collections. No October nationwide retail-registration total is asserted.
Maruti Suzuki's 2,76,120 total contains exports (49,872), supplies to other OEMs (9,459), and domestic PV/LCV sales (2,16,789). It is not domestic passenger-car retail.

Mahindra's 73,338 figure is domestic utility vehicles, including its EV subsidiary; the company's broader 1,31,109 total spans other vehicle categories and exports. These scopes cannot be directly compared with Maruti's total or summed as an industry total.
Mahindra's newsroom page displays a publication date of 2 November 2026, while the release text is dated 1 November 2026. Both dates are disclosed rather than silently harmonised.

The five checks, metrics and 15-minute exercise are RPHV editorial recommendations, not OEM statistics, official benchmarks or a projection of profitability. Stock ageing cut-offs are practical local management choices, not industry standards.

issues.title: AI is entering aftersales. Fix the repair handoff first.
issues.summary: An Indian commercial-vehicle maker has launched an AI-enabled service coordination system. The lesson for every dealership is practical: make each repair's next action, owner and promised time visible before buying another dashboard.
issues.sourceNote: VECV / Eicher Power Solutions announcement dated 13 October 2026. Company-reported connected-platform counts at the time of announcement; no monthly measurement window stated. This is NOT wholesale dispatch data or retail registrations.

metrics.label: Connected vehicles claimed
metrics.context: My Eicher platform; company statement, 13 Oct 2026

metrics.label: Customers supported claimed
metrics.context: My Eicher platform; company statement, 13 Oct 2026

metrics.label: Date of service-platform launch
metrics.context: 2026; original corporate announcement

issues.reportingType: Company product-launch announcement and self-reported platform scale; neither OEM wholesales nor customer retail registrations.
intro: On 13 October 2026, VE Commercial Vehicles announced an expanded AI-enabled uptime service model for its Eicher trucks and buses. It described a central control tower for service coordination and a generative-AI tool intended to help mechanics and diagnostic teams.

The company also reported that its My Eicher app supports more than 200,000 customers and connects over 460,000 vehicles. These are company-stated platform totals, not an independent survey, vehicle sales figures or proof that workshop turnaround has improved.

The useful dealership question is simple: can an adviser, technician, parts executive and customer all see who must do what next on a delayed job? Better visibility, clear ownership and timely escalation are worth testing before a costly technology rollout.

interpretation.heading: The operational lesson: close the handoff gap
points: Start with delayed or repeat repair orders. Record the current block, next action, accountable person and promised update time in one visible place.
Use diagnostic help tools to assist trained technicians, not to bypass manufacturer procedures, safety precautions or technical verification.
Measure first-time-right results and communication reliability before attributing improvements to AI. The announcement does not disclose audited changes in these outcomes.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Complete the after-sales handover
desks.check: Check five recent deliveries: was the customer shown how to book service, report a concern and reach roadside support where provided?
desks.metric: Deliveries with documented service onboarding / total deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: Ownership support should be clear before the first problem arises.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Give every blocked repair one owner
desks.check: Review five delayed or repeat-concern ROs; log the next action, named owner, customer-update deadline and escalation path.
desks.metric: Open ROs with owner + next action + update time / all open ROs (%)
desks.rationale: A dashboard cannot rescue a job nobody owns.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Replace vague parts status with evidence
desks.check: For each parts-blocked RO, record verified part number, order status, supplier confirmation and realistic ETA.
desks.metric: Parts-blocked ROs with confirmed status and ETA / all parts-blocked ROs (%)
desks.rationale: A credible ETA makes service promises more dependable.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Carry repair history into appraisal
desks.check: Check whether trade-in inspection records include warning lamps, diagnosis, pending repairs and realistic reconditioning cost.
desks.metric: Appraisals with complete diagnostic and repair-cost sheet / appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: Unrecorded repair risks become unexpected resale expenses.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace money stuck behind open jobs
desks.check: Pick service invoices or claims awaiting settlement; identify the missing approval, document or owner and expected clearance date.
desks.metric: Value of service receivables outstanding over 30 days (INR)
desks.rationale: A repaired vehicle does not create usable cash until the billing and collection loop closes.

issues.huddleTitle: Five desks. Five exceptions. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Each function brings one real case with an incomplete handoff. Record the blocker, next action, owner and deadline in a shared log; recheck the same five cases tomorrow.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: find one delivery with incomplete service onboarding; assign a callback.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: select one delayed or repeat RO; name the next action and customer-update time.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: confirm a blocked repair part and realistic ETA, or document that none is available.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: identify one appraisal with an unresolved diagnostic or repair-cost risk.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: take one ageing claim or invoice; assign its resolution owner and deadline.
limitations: This is a single commercial-vehicle manufacturer's announcement, not a representative measure of India's passenger-vehicle or two-wheeler aftersales market.

The platform scale of over 200,000 customers and more than 460,000 connected vehicles is company-reported as of the 13 October 2026 announcement; it has no disclosed monthly measurement window or independent audit.
The release provides no independently verified before/after result for workshop turnaround, first-time-right repair or customer satisfaction; do not claim such improvements are proven.
No vehicle wholesale, dealer retail-registration or market-share figures are used in this issue. The five suggested checks and metrics are RPHV editorial recommendations, not OEM benchmarks.
Technician safety, authorisations and vehicle-specific diagnosis must follow manufacturer documentation and applicable regulations; AI-generated advice is not a substitute.

issues.title: Wholesales are up. Are dealership processes keeping pace?
issues.summary: India's passenger-vehicle dispatches rose sharply in July–September 2026. Strong factory-to-dealer movement is useful context—but it cannot, on its own, tell a dealer whether enquiries are converting, vehicles are moving or cash is being released.
issues.sourceNote: SIAM, published 15 October 2026; reporting period July–September 2026. The figures are manufacturer domestic sales/wholesales, not customer retail registrations.

metrics.label: Passenger vehicles, domestic sales
metrics.context: SIAM • July–September 2026 • wholesales

metrics.label: Passenger vehicle growth
metrics.context: Against July–September 2025 • SIAM

metrics.label: Utility-vehicle share of PV sales
metrics.context: July–September 2026 • SIAM

issues.reportingType: OEM-to-dealer domestic sales (wholesale); not retail registrations
intro: A strong market headline is a starting point, not a dealership performance report. On 15 October 2026, SIAM reported 13,60,687 passenger-vehicle domestic sales for the July–September quarter, 30.7% higher than the corresponding period of FY2025–26.

Those numbers describe manufacturer domestic dispatches—commonly called wholesales. Customer retail registrations are a separate measure. A dealership can see healthy vehicle inflow while still carrying excess stock, facing delayed deliveries or struggling to convert enquiries into invoices.

For the operations team, the right response is not to celebrate or panic on one industry number. It is to reconcile the market signal with the dealership's own pipeline, workshop load, inventory exposure and collection cycle.

interpretation.heading: What this means on the ground
points: Compare confirmed customer orders and registrations with new arrivals rather than treating dispatches as retail demand.
Review ageing units and delivery readiness before accepting that higher inventory automatically improves sales.
Connect expected vehicle parc growth with technician readiness, genuine parts supply and service retention—but do not infer service demand directly from one quarter's wholesales.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check delivery readiness, not just bookings
desks.check: Take the next seven days' booked deliveries. Confirm allocation, finance clearance, accessories, promised date and registration progress.
desks.metric: Delivery-ready bookings ÷ bookings due in 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: A booking is not yet a delivered car. Measure the handover pipeline.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Make promised delivery dates visible
desks.check: Review all open repair orders with their promised completion times. Identify jobs blocked by diagnosis, approvals, parts or capacity.
desks.metric: ROs delivered within promise ÷ total delivered ROs (%)
desks.rationale: Customer confidence depends on reliable service completion, not only inflow.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Expose cash sitting in ageing stock
desks.check: List parts untouched for 90 days, then check demand, supersession, reservations and return possibilities before reordering.
desks.metric: Value of stock aged 90+ days ÷ total stock value (%)
desks.rationale: A growing market is not a reason to relax inventory discipline.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Protect margin before acquisition
desks.check: For each proposed exchange, record ownership checks, repair inspection, reconditioning estimate and realistic resale value.
desks.metric: Acquisitions with approved margin sheet ÷ total acquisitions (%)
desks.rationale: Purchase price alone is not the acquisition cost.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Reconcile blocked money daily
desks.check: Trace unmatched receipts, delayed customer balances and pending manufacturer credits to a named owner and an expected resolution date.
desks.metric: Unreconciled receipts and claims older than 7 days (count)
desks.rationale: Turnover improves financial health only when cash and claims are controlled.

issues.huddleTitle: One blocked item. One owner. One deadline.
issues.huddleSummary: Each desk brings one exception that is holding up a delivery, repair, payment or stock decision. Close the huddle with a named owner and next action.
huddle: Minutes 0–3: Sales identifies one promised delivery at risk and checks the evidence.
Minutes 3–6: Service identifies one repair order that may miss its promise.
Minutes 6–9: Spares identifies one order or item whose status is unclear.
Minutes 9–12: Used Cars or Accounts identifies one margin or collection exception.
Minutes 12–15: Assign one owner and deadline to every unresolved exception.
limitations: SIAM's July–September PV domestic-sales data exclude BMW, Mercedes, JLR and Volvo Auto, as indicated in the release notes.
Wholesale dispatches do not equal customer retail registrations, and neither measure establishes any individual dealer's profitability.
The five department checks and suggested metrics are RPHV editorial recommendations, not published SIAM benchmarks.
